resolvedQuestions.text: RQ-1: Which scripts, tests, generators, runtime adapters and other tools read a SKILL.md MACHINE ROUTER section or its markers, and what sibling ROUTER.md change does each require?
RQ-6.1: What exactly does the freshness signature in runtime/lib/freshness.ts hash, and does a router move out of SKILL.md leave a stale checkout looking fresh?
RQ-2: How do Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, Pi, Devin and Hermes load a skill, and do they load sibling files automatically? What does the Hermes copy step include?
RQ-6.2: How does runtime/scripts/skill_advisor_runtime.py discover and parse a skill, and what must change for it to read a sibling ROUTER.md?
RQ-3: Which machine-router facts does an agent need in context at runtime, which facts only scripts need, and what pointer must remain in SKILL.md?
RQ-6.3: What does the skill graph compiler in runtime/lib/skill-graph/ index and embed, and does it parse SKILL.md body text, Keywords comments or router markers?
RQ-4: How can a hub MACHINE ROUTER join its existing root ROUTER.md without changing the router replay mode projection?
RQ-6.4: What reads the leaf inventory, leaf-manifest.config.json and leaf-scopes, and does the router move change any of them?
RQ-5: What migration preserves advisor accuracy 155/195, 49/66 and 19/24, router replay and compiled-route hashes while measuring token savings per skill and tracking debt?
RQ-6.5: Does any scorer lane read SKILL.md body text, keywords comments or router markers, and does the router move change scores or accuracy?
RQ-6.6: What do the advisor hooks, the plugin bridges and the routing-accuracy baseline scripts depend on, and what is the fix for each?

keyFindings.text: The freshness signature probes exactly two files per skill, `SKILL.md` and `graph-metadata.json`, and folds both into one hash; a `ROUTER.md` edit alone leaves the signature byte-identical, so `deriveFreshness` returns `live` against a graph that no longer matches the router. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:164] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:168] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:177-178] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:278-287]

The package checker parses H2 sections and fenced machine assignments from SKILL.md. It requires the MACHINE ROUTER appendix to be final, and the SMART ROUTING marker check includes the appendix body. Moving the block therefore changes both structural and marker validation. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py:815-906] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py:1162-1169]

The doc-frontmatter harvest cannot pick up a root `ROUTER.md` either, because it walks only `references/` and `assets/` and is additionally gated off by default behind an env flag. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/doc-frontmatter.ts:170] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/doc-frontmatter.ts:42-46]

The leaf inventory is root-scoped, so a sibling `ROUTER.md` is not a leaf and the two generated artifacts stay byte-stable: `leafRoots` names five subdirectories and a root-level file is outside all of them, and `leaf-scopes.json` repeats the same root-scoped leaf list. The only leaf-side change is prose: the config's `_note` states the router is "the in-SKILL.md INTENT_SIGNALS + RESOURCE_MAP router", which goes stale the moment the router file moves. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/leaf-manifest.config.json:4] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/leaf-manifest.config.json:7] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/leaf-scopes.json:1-13]

`ROUTER.md` is already a governed root file, but only a hub's copy is validated: the metadata contract lists it in `METADATA_FILES`, requires it for the hub class, and does not forbid it for the standalone class, while the checker runs the root-router contract inside a `CLASS_HUB` guard. system-skill-advisor declares neither `mode-registry.json` nor `hub-router.json`, so it classifies standalone and a relocated `ROUTER.md` there would be neither required, forbidden, nor checked. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/lib/skill-root-metadata-contract.cjs:46-55] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/lib/skill-root-metadata-contract.cjs:75-108] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs:688-694]

No advisor code parses the MACHINE ROUTER section. A package-wide search for that phrase matches only the section heading and the pointer sentence that announces it, and a search for the `router.md` filename inside the scoring runtime matches only the doc-file demotion rules, never a reader of the section. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/SKILL.md:61] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/SKILL.md:220]

No live scorer lane reads `SKILL.md` body text, and the five lane weights are stable inputs to any before/after measurement: the explicit lane scores `intentSignals` and `keywords`, the lexical lane scores name, description, domains, `intentSignals` and `keywords`, BM25 weights those same fields, the derived lane scores `derivedTriggers` and `derivedKeywords`, and the semantic-shadow lane scores `description`. The explicit lane already treats `router.md` as a doc filename in both the doc-file suffix guard and the write-verb doc list, and the Python scorer mirrors it, so the new filename needs no lane change and a prompt like "edit ROUTER.md" is already demoted out of skill mention. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:230] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:314] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py:3019-3021]

The one real accuracy hazard is an alias, not a file read: `'smart router'` is hard-mapped to `sk-code` at 0.65 in the explicit lane, so a migration-shaped prompt that names the machine router can be captured by the code hub before the advisor's own vocabulary is consulted. This has to be replayed against the corpus rather than reasoned about. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/explicit.ts:187]

Derived extraction does read the whole body, code blocks included, but its writer is off the serving path and the fleet producer preserves curated fields, so the committed `derived` block does not move unless someone re-runs the deprecated extractor. Reading the body feeds headings, body ngrams and code-block ngrams into the buckets, and `SKILL.md` enters `sourceDocs`, `keyFiles` and the provenance dependency set. The hooks carry freshness, never content: the Claude hook and the CLI-fallback helper both read `freshness` out of the advisor envelope and branch on `live`/`stale`/`absent`/`unavailable`, and the Pi extension is a symlink to the hook file inside the skill, so there is one Pi source to change, not two. The three quoted accuracy numbers are a reproducible baseline, not a survey: they are recorded with the exact corpus, holdout and ambiguity sha256 values, the empty-database and filesystem-projection environment, and the capture commit, so the migration can be measured as a delta against the same inputs rather than re-argued. The recorded values are 155/195 at 0.7949, 49/66 at 0.7424, and 19/24 at 0.7917 with tau 0.03. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/scorer-eval-baseline.json:1-46]

Router replay reads SKILL.md and parses INTENT_SIGNALS, RESOURCE_MAP and DEFAULT_RESOURCE from its text. Its fallback follows a references/ markdown pointer, then tries hub-router.json, but it does not currently resolve a root sibling ROUTER.md. verify-router-sync calls this same parser. The per-skill fingerprint loop is keyed on `SKILL.md` existing: `if (!skillMd) continue` skips the slug entirely, so a skill whose router moved out is still enumerated, but a skill whose `SKILL.md` were reduced to a stub or removed would vanish from `skillFingerprints` and from `maxSourceMtimeMs`. A fix therefore has to add `ROUTER.md` as a third `addSignaturePart` probe while keeping the `missing` marker, not replace the `SKILL.md` probe. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:162-179] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:131-137]

The corpus driver runs the Python scorer as a subprocess rather than an in-process API, so any change to discovery or frontmatter parsing shows up as a baseline movement, while a pure `ROUTER.md` move does not. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/score-routing-corpus.py:27-35]

The stage-two replay that already reads a root `ROUTER.md` enumerates hubs only, so a standalone skill's relocated router would be replayed by nothing; whether a standalone skill is allowed a root `ROUTER.md` at all is a policy question the root-router contract's own header reserves for parent hubs. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/leaf-route-replay.cjs:320-330] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/lib/root-router-contract.cjs:7-19]

The mtime fallback in the same file is only reachable when no stored `sourceSignature` exists, and it compares `maxSourceMtimeMs` against the SQLite artifact; a moved router adds no mtime to that maximum, so the fallback path has the same blind spot as the signature path. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/freshness.ts:290-298]

The optional dead-route check reads each live SKILL.md and extracts fenced RESOURCE_MAP or DEFAULT_RESOURCE paths. The measurement parser also reads SKILL.md before extracting the router model, so both need a sibling-file resolver if those declarations leave the skill body. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/scripts/verify_alignment_drift.py:815-839] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/scripts/verify_alignment_drift.py:842-879] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/observability/smart-router-measurement.ts:517-544]

The doctor parent check independently parses the same final section and rejects a packet-local ROUTER.md. The routing-shape tests also assert appendix location, finality and marker discovery, so the package gate, doctor gate and their fixtures must move together. The OpenCode plugin bridge carries a second, independent implementation of the same signature, hashing `skill:<slug>:SKILL.md` and `graph-metadata.json` plus four `implementation:` paths, so a `ROUTER.md` probe has to be added in both places or the plugin and the daemon will disagree about whether the graph is live. [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/system-skill-advisor.js:330-344] [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/system-skill-advisor.js:142-156]

Both skill-generation workflows still instruct authors to put packet machine routing in the final SKILL.md section, while both structural gates forbid a ROUTER.md inside mode packets. This conflicts with a blanket move of every skill to a sibling ROUTER.md. LOGIC-SYNC REQUIRED is recorded: the migration needs an explicit canon change or a narrowed eligibility rule. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-skill-auto.yaml:347] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/create/assets/create-skill-parent-auto.yaml:476] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/package_skill.py:1004-1009]

The daemon watcher never sees a `ROUTER.md` write: `discoverWatchTargets` pushes a `skill-md` target, a `graph-metadata` target, its derived key files, and optional doc-frontmatter targets, but no router target, so even a corrected signature would not be recomputed on the event that changed routing. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/daemon/watcher.ts:263-286]

Python-side discovery and parsing are router-blind by construction, which is why the move does not break them: `_discover_skill_files` joins `SKILL.md` and requires it to exist, and `parse_frontmatter_fast` reads the frontmatter block, then only the leading HTML comments, merging a `<!-- Keywords: ... -->` comment, and returns at the first content line, so the MACHINE ROUTER body was never in scope. The leaf-manifest generator walks configured resource roots and does not parse SKILL.md router declarations. Compiled-routing inputs do attest whole source bytes, so the relocated ROUTER.md must enter the source identity and hash set even when the selected route projection stays unchanged. The Python record cache is invalidated by mtime and size of the discovered `SKILL.md` files only, so it also cannot see a `ROUTER.md` change; this is harmless only because the parser reads no router content, and becomes a defect the moment the parser is widened to read `ROUTER.md`. The graph compiler reads only `graph-metadata.json`: it discovers `graph-metadata.json` per skill directory and compiles from those, with no `SKILL.md` read anywhere in the file, so the compiled graph shape is unchanged by the move, and only the `derived` payload carried inside each metadata file could change. Embeddings are description-only, so vectors are unaffected: `skillDescriptionForEmbedding` reads `SKILL.md` frontmatter `description` and nothing else, and that helper feeds the `skill_nodes.embedding` column at both write sites. Workspace delivery differs by runtime: Claude, OpenCode, Pi, and Devin expose the canonical skills tree through directory symlinks; Hermes builds standalone SKILL.md copies; Codex has no .codex/skills tree; Cursor has no .cursor/skills tree but current Cursor docs also discover .claude/skills, which this checkout links to .skilled/skills. The local Cursor manifest records only its own skills location, so refresh that description alongside the migration. The skill runtimes use progressive loading: they advertise metadata or a description, then load SKILL.md when selected; supporting-file contents are read only when the instructions call for them. OpenCode states this explicitly, while Claude, Pi, Cursor, and Codex document the same on-demand pattern. A sibling ROUTER.md therefore needs an explicit path and read instruction in SKILL.md; directory presence alone does not put its text in the model context. This checkout does not provision a Codex-native skills directory: its Codex sync manifest says there is no .codex/skills, and the root AGENTS.md routes through the skill-advisor hook or explicit advisor CLI. OpenAI documents repo-local Codex skills under .agents/skills, but that root is not present in this checkout; treat Codex loading here as explicit canonical-path routing, not automatic project skill discovery. The Hermes sync walks only files named SKILL.md, writes one generated markdown file per skill, and rewrites relative Markdown links to point back to the canonical skill directory. It deliberately excludes references, scripts, assets, and other sibling files, so a relocated ROUTER.md will not be in the Hermes preload copy; the generator must either add that one sidecar or rewrite the pointer to its canonical .skilled path. Agents still need the intent-selection rule, exact route destinations, load levels, and low-confidence or ambiguity fallback when they choose skill resources; the canonical smart-router template explicitly describes discovery, path guards, conditional loads, a runtime key, and fallback as router behavior. Literal delimiters and assignment shapes are also consumed by replay, validation, measurement, and package tooling, but those parsers should read the sidecar directly instead of requiring the script syntax to remain inside SKILL.md. The pointer policy conflicts with the current authoring template statement that mode packets never carry ROUTER.md, so the authoring template, creation workflows, parser checks, and tests must be revised together before migration. ruledOutDirections.text: Adding a lane for router markers. No lane has a field for them, and the projection exposes only frontmatter, keywords, metadata signals and the derived block.
Adding `ROUTER.md` to the doc-frontmatter harvest. The harvest walks `references/` and `assets/` only and is off by default.
Treating the graph compiler as a body reader. The file has no `SKILL.md` read; it copies `graph-metadata.json` as authored.

Treating the derived lane as a live body consumer. Its writer is marked deprecated and off the serving path, and the fleet producer preserves curated trigger and topic fields while pruning only dead paths.
Treating the leaf-manifest generator as a direct MACHINE ROUTER reader. Its source walks configured leaf roots and does not parse SKILL.md.
Treating every root ROUTER.md parser as a current reader of the SKILL.md appendix. The root-router checks read the separate stage-two router; their merge behavior is examined in RQ-4.
